6797.name: Justin Herbert
6797.headline: Finger not broken; expected to start MNF at Baltimore
6797.news: Herbert went 13-of-23 for 193 yards, one TD and one INT in the Nov. 8 44-22 loss to Houston. He was sacked a career-high eight times, and his 58-yard TD to Quentin Johnston ended a 37-drive touchdown drought for the offense. He left in the fourth quarter with an injury to his left (non-throwing) middle finger, and DJ Uiagalelei finished the game. On Nov. 9, Jim Harbaugh said X-rays were negative and that Herbert should be good to go for Week 10 on Monday night at Baltimore. The Chargers are 0-8.
6797.take: The finger isn't the problem. The problem is an offense that gave up eight sacks and went 37 drives without a touchdown before that late score. Week 9 came to roughly 11-12 fantasy points, and a road game against Baltimore doesn't project much better, so he's a sit in 12-team 1QB. In superflex dynasty he's 28 and his value is at its lowest, so a 1-6 rebuilding team should hold him and not sell for less than QB1 value.

6904.name: Jalen Hurts
6904.headline: Still on IR with blood clots; expected out for 2026
6904.news: Hurts remains on IR. The Eagles and his agent announced on Oct. 19 that an ultrasound in London before Week 5 first found a superficial clot, and further testing then found deep vein thrombosis with clots in both lungs, which explains the conflicting reports. Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter reported that he's expected to miss the rest of the season, though the team hasn't formally ruled him out. He's on blood thinners for at least three months, and the Eagles call his prognosis very good and expect a full recovery. Philadelphia made no QB move at the Nov. 10 deadline, is 2-7 and has a Week 10 bye.
6904.take: The reports don't really conflict: the superficial clot was the first finding, and the DVT with clots in both lungs is the current diagnosis. In redraft he's a drop unless you have an open IR spot. In dynasty, a medical issue isn't a decline in skill and the team expects a full recovery, so he should be Philadelphia's 2027 starter. Contenders get nothing from him this year, so his trade price is at its lowest; a 1-6 rebuilding team should hold and try to buy if anyone will sell cheap.

12491.take: Kiner should get the most volume in Week 10, since only Larison is behind him, so in 12-team half-PPR he's a volume-based flex. A matchup against Detroit and an unproven back with a thin offensive line keep his ceiling modest. This is a one-week window before the bye, and Stevenson could be back for Week 12. In dynasty he's a short-term opportunity rather than a long-term piece, so pick him up for free but don't trade anything meaningful for him.
12491.handcuff: Lan Larison is the only other healthy RB and would take whatever Kiner doesn't; Stevenson could be back for Week 12 after the bye.

4017.name: Deshaun Watson
4017.headline: Back from concussion, starting Week 10 against Houston
4017.news: Watson missed Cleveland's Week 9 loss at New Orleans with a concussion, and Shedeur Sanders started in his place. On Nov. 9, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that the Browns planned to go back to Watson for Week 10 despite Sanders' solid game, though Todd Monken hadn't named a starter at that point. Watson had already been cleared from the concussion protocol, and Monken announced on Nov. 11 that Watson will start Sunday, Nov. 15, at home against his former team, Houston. One report says a loss could reopen the competition after Cleveland's bye.
4017.take: He has the job back for now, but the leash looks short, and Sanders playing well in relief means one bad game could cost him the start after the bye. Houston's defense is a tough matchup, so he's not a start in 12-team 1QB; superflex managers can use him only as a low-end QB2. In dynasty he's 31, has had several injuries and has no secure future as a starter, so a rebuilding team should sell him to any contender who needs QB depth.
points: Short leash; job could reopen after bye

In 12-team redraft he's a boom-or-bust WR4/flex, not a weekly starter, so hold him.
